summary: Step 4: default-reject review by a different model (reimplementers, proof referees, literature recheck)

v.own_numbers: Instance r=8000, a=(12871,12875,12921,20863,20986), F=7. Exact full-coefficient brute force (three independent implementations in /tmp/claude-0/qu/review/r3/N3_nearmiss_tb-A/: uni.py / uni2.py = Python big-int Kronecker substitution with 128-bit slots and checksum sum(c)=prod(a)*b; uni.c = C exact sliding-window product with unsigned __int128 coefficients; chk2.gp = PARI/GP polynomial product) all give: b=1..8 weakly unimodal (Y), b=9..13 NOT weakly unimodal. U ∩ [1,13] = {1,...,8}, exactly as claimed. (Degree of P_13 is 176511; max coefficient ~4e17 so int64/128-bit exact.)
v.reasons: The claimed result U ∩ [1,13] = {1,...,8} for r=8000, a=(12871,12875,12921,20863,20986) reproduces exactly under three independently written exact implementations (Python big-int, C 128-bit sliding window, PARI/GP), all written from the text description alone. Twenty additional out-of-range instances (other r from 1 to 50000, k from 3 to 8, a_i up to 130002) were computed by exact brute force; C and Python agree wherever both were run, and no inconsistency with the claimed pattern (U an initial segment containing {1,...,F+1}, with the near-miss instance tight at b=F+1=8) was found. Checksums (sum of coefficients = prod(a_i)*b, all coefficients < 2^120) passed in every run.

v.own_numbers: Independent implementation (exact Python-int sliding-window products in /tmp/claude-0/qu/review/r3/N3_nearmiss_tb-B/check.py, cross-checked by a second numpy int64 convolution implementation np_check.py; max coefficient 3.36e16, no overflow): for r=8000, a=(12871,12875,12921,20863,20986), P_b is weakly unimodal for b=1..8 (peak at index 40256+8000(b-1), no violation) and NOT unimodal for b=9..13 (last ascent ends at index 68933, first descent at 68933->68934, later re-ascent up to index 75577 for b=9, 83577 for b=10, ..., i.e. first violation at index ~72256). So U ∩ [1,13] = {1,...,8}, exactly as claimed. Side facts: D = 80511, F = 1+1+1+2+2 = 7, so the cutoff is b = F+1 = 8. Unimodality routine validated against brute-force definition and sympy polynomial expansion on 200 random small (r,a,b) instances (small_check.py), all agreeing.
v.new_instances_tested: Tested b = 14..20 (7 new values outside the claimed range) with both implementations: all non-unimodal, with the same dip at index 68933 and a re-ascent reaching 8000(b-1)+11577, consistent with the set U being the initial segment {1..8} for these parameters. Also 200 random small instances (r in 2..5, k in 1..3, a_i in 1..7, b in 1..5) to validate the coefficient and unimodality code against sympy and the brute-force definition.
v.reasons: Both an exact Python big-int implementation and an independent numpy int64 implementation (overflow checked) reproduce exactly the claimed set U ∩ [1,13] = {1,...,8}: P_b unimodal for b<=8, non-unimodal for b=9..13 (genuine dip at coefficient index 68933 followed by a later rise). The unimodality checker was validated against sympy and the brute-force definition on 200 small random cases. New instances b=14..20 behave consistently (all non-unimodal). No mismatch found.
